bill.title: EASE Act
bill.latestActionText: Read twice and referred to the Committee on Finance.
bill.officialSummary: Ensuring Access to Specialty Care Everywhere Act or the EASE Act This bill requires the Center for Medicare and Medicaid Innovation (CMMI) to test a model that uses a network of providers to remotely furnish specialty health care to Medicare, Medicaid, and Children's Health Insurance Program (CHIP) beneficiaries in rural areas. To conduct the model, the CMMI must select at least one provider network that is a nonprofit entity and that consists of at least 50 federally qualified health centers, rural health clinics, critical access hospitals, or rural emergency hospitals. At least half of the providers in the network must be located in rural areas. Providers must use digital methods (e.g., telehealth technology) to provide specialty care and must coordinate with beneficiaries' primary care providers.

classification.plainSummary: This bill directs the Center for Medicare and Medicaid Innovation to test a program that uses networks of rural health providers to deliver specialty medical care remotely to Medicare, Medicaid, and CHIP patients in rural areas. The networks must include at least 50 qualifying rural clinics or hospitals, be nonprofit, and use telehealth technology to connect patients with specialists while coordinating with their primary care doctors. At least half of the providers in each network must be located in rural areas.

industries.rationale: The bill directly establishes a payment model for federally qualified health centers, rural health clinics, critical access hospitals, and rural emergency hospitals to furnish specialty care services.
The bill requires digital methods and telehealth technology to deliver remote specialty care, creating demand for broadband and telecommunications infrastructure in rural areas.
The bill's reliance on telehealth platforms and digital coordination systems would affect vendors providing health IT and telemedicine software solutions.
The bill modifies service delivery and reimbursement models for Medicare, Medicaid, and CHIP, which may affect how insurers and managed-care organizations structure networks and payments.

plain.whatItDoes: This bill would require the Center for Medicare and Medicaid Innovation to test a model that uses a network of providers to remotely furnish specialty health care to Medicare, Medicaid, and Children's Health Insurance Program beneficiaries in rural areas.
plain.whoItTouches: Anyone who sees a doctor or pays for care.
plain.everydayEffect: If it passed, the change would show up in getting care, and paying for it. Nothing has changed yet. Most bills never become law.

disclaimer: This tool places two public records next to each other: who donated to a member of Congress, and what that member legislated on. Any overlap you see is a correlation, not causation. It is not evidence of a quid pro quo, of influence, or of wrongdoing. Legislators routinely receive support from industries in their district for the same reason they legislate on them: those industries are there.
